titleText.es: Si pensáis que esto es muy duro con la crítica literaria, leed el artículo de la Wikipedia sobre la deconstrucción.
titleText.en: If you think this is too hard on literary criticism, read the Wikipedia article on deconstruction.
titleText.noteEn: The Spanish archive closely translates the official English title text and uses the informal plural forms pensáis and leed that are common in Spain.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: to sit down; to sit myself down
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Sentar means “to seat.” With the matching small word me attached, sentarme normally means that the speaker sits down. The attached me does not need a separate English word.

example.es: Voy a sentarme aquí.
example.en: I am going to sit down here.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: A posgrado is advanced study pursued after completing an initial university degree.

example.es: Hace un posgrado en historia.
example.en: She is doing graduate studies in history.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: to time; to count how long
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Contar often means “to count” or “to tell.” When it is followed by cuánto tardar, it can mean measuring or timing how long something takes.

example.es: La profesora va a contar cuánto tardan en ordenar las tarjetas.
example.en: The teacher is going to time how long they take to sort the cards.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Su stays singular because the possessed thing is singular, even when the owners are several people. Sus is used before a plural possessed thing.

example.es: Los alumnos conocen su materia.
example.en: The students know their subject.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Materia can mean physical matter, but in education it means a subject or area of knowledge.

example.es: La física es su materia favorita.
example.en: Physics is her favorite subject.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: In engineering, disipación describes unwanted energy, especially heat, being spread out and removed from a system.

example.es: El ventilador mejora la disipación de calor.
example.en: The fan improves heat dissipation.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Probado is probar's completed-action form. After a form of haber, it asks or states whether an option has been tried.

example.es: ¿Habéis probado otra solución?
example.en: Have you all tried another solution?

cardDefinitions.noteEn: A logarithm answers what exponent is needed to produce a given number from a chosen base.

example.es: Estudiamos logaritmos en matemáticas.
example.en: We study logarithms in mathematics.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Lingüística is the systematic study of language and how languages work.

example.es: Estudia lingüística en la universidad.
example.en: She studies linguistics at university.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Ugrofinesa describes the branch of the Uralic language family that includes Finnish, Estonian, and Hungarian. It uses feminine singular -a to match familia.

example.es: El finés es una lengua ugrofinesa.
example.en: Finnish is a Finno-Ugric language.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Incluye is the present form of incluir used with one person, thing, group, or category.

example.es: El precio incluye el desayuno.
example.en: The price includes breakfast.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: no separate English word; a + el before the named language
cardDefinitions.noteEn: The printed al combines a and el before the specifically named language. Natural English simply names the language after “include.”

example.es: El grupo incluye al dialecto local.
example.en: The group includes the local dialect.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Before a noun, último can mean the final or last remaining one, or simply the most recent one. The surrounding noun and situation distinguish those readings: el último superviviente is the last survivor, while mi último trabajo can mean my latest work.

example.es: Leí su último artículo.
example.en: I read his latest article.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Consiste is a present form of consistir. Spanish normally follows it with en before the defining activity or components.

example.es: El trabajo consiste en comparar datos.
example.en: The work consists of comparing data.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: of; introduces what something consists of
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Spanish uses consistir en before the activity or components. English normally uses “consist of.”

example.es: La prueba consiste en ordenar las piezas.
example.en: The test consists of arranging the pieces.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Clasificar can mean placing things in categories or arranging them by a ranking.

example.es: Van a clasificar los resultados de mejor a peor.
example.en: They are going to rank the results from best to worst.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: from; marks the start of a range
cardDefinitions.noteEn: In the paired pattern de ... a ..., de introduces the starting point and a introduces the endpoint.

example.es: Ordena las notas de la mejor a la peor.
example.en: Order the grades from best to worst.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: to; marks the end of a range
cardDefinitions.noteEn: In the paired pattern de ... a ..., de introduces the starting point and a introduces the endpoint.

example.es: Ordena las notas de la mejor a la peor.
example.en: Order the grades from best to worst.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: With el, la, los, or las, peor normally means “worst.” Without an article it often means “worse.”

example.es: Esa fue la peor opción.
example.en: That was the worst option.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Crítica can name the activity or field of analyzing and evaluating art, literature, or ideas.

example.es: Estudia crítica de cine.
example.en: She studies film criticism.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Literaria describes something related to literature and uses feminine singular -a with a noun such as crítica.

example.es: Publicó una revista literaria.
example.en: She published a literary magazine.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: In literary theory, deconstrucción is an approach that examines tensions, assumptions, and unstable contrasts within a text.

example.es: El ensayo aplica la deconstrucción al texto.
example.en: The essay applies deconstruction to the text.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Inextricable describes things connected so tightly that they cannot be separated or untangled.

example.es: Los dos problemas son inextricables.
example.en: The two problems are inextricable.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: No combines with solo to introduce the first part of the paired contrast no solo ... sino ....

example.es: No solo llamó, sino que vino.
example.en: She not only called, but also came.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: After no, solo marks the first item in a contrast that later adds another item with sino.

example.es: No solo llamó, sino que vino.
example.en: She not only called, but also came.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: but also; introduces the added contrast after no solo
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Sino introduces the second noun, description, or matching phrase after no solo. Before a full changed verb, Spanish commonly uses sino que.

example.es: No solo estudia física, sino química.
example.en: She studies not only physics, but also chemistry.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Ser usually appears as the dictionary form “to be.” With an article, el ser can instead be a noun meaning a being, existence, or the self.

example.es: El ensayo reflexiona sobre el ser.
example.en: The essay reflects on being.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: academic papers; research articles (informal English borrowing)
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Spanish often prefers artículos or trabajos académicos. In academic conversation, the English borrowing paper is also used informally; its plural is papers.

example.es: Publicó dos papers sobre astronomía.
example.en: She published two academic papers on astronomy.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: no separate English word; marks percatarse, “to notice”
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Percatarse uses a matching small word: me, te, se, nos, or os. Se is used with él, ella, usted, ellos, ellas, or ustedes.

example.es: Ellos se percataron del error.
example.en: They noticed the error.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Percatado is percatarse's completed-action form. With se and a form of haber, it says that someone has noticed or realized something.

example.es: Los técnicos se han percatado del error.
example.en: The technicians have noticed the error.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you say that someone sits down with another person or group?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use a matching form of sentarse, then con before the person or group.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: The short word matches the person who sits: me, te, se, nos, or os. With a changed present-time verb, it comes before: me siento, te sientas, se sienta. With the unchanged dictionary form, attach it: sentarme, sentarte, sentarse, sentarnos, or sentaros. Con stays unchanged and introduces the companion or group.

example.es: Hoy me siento con Ana durante el almuerzo.
example.en: Today I sit down with Ana during lunch.

cardDefinitions.promptEs: tardar + tiempo + en + acción en forma de diccionario
cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you say how long someone takes to do an action?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use a form of tardar, optionally give the amount of time, then en and the action in its unchanged dictionary form.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: The action form ends in -ar, -er, or -ir and can carry an attached pronoun: tardaron una hora en llegar; tardan mucho en darse cuenta. Use cuánto to ask the amount of time.

example.es: Tardaron dos horas en llegar.
example.en: They took two hours to arrive.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you say that someone is an expert in a subject or field?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use a form of ser, experto or experta, and en before the field.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Experto changes to match the person: experto, experta, expertos, or expertas. The field can be a noun or an action used as a noun.

example.es: Ana es experta en lingüística.
example.en: Ana is an expert in linguistics.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: Klingon is a constructed fictional language from Star Trek, not a member of the Finno-Ugric language family
cardDefinitions.noteEn: The Finno-Ugric branch includes real languages such as Finnish, Estonian, and Hungarian. Suggesting Klingon as another member exposes that the speaker is bluffing about linguistics.

cardDefinitions.promptEs: consistir en + acción en forma de diccionario
cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you say what an activity or process consists of doing?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use a form of consistir, then en and the action verb in its unchanged dictionary form.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: The unchanged action form ends in -ar, -er, or -ir: consiste en comparar, aprender, or decidir. English normally says “consists of doing.”

example.es: La tarea consiste en comparar dos textos.
example.en: The task consists of comparing two texts.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you express a range from one endpoint to another?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Put de before the starting point and a before the endpoint.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Articles and other determiners stay with each endpoint: de la mejor a la peor; del lunes al viernes. The same frame works for rankings, places, and times.

example.es: Trabaja de lunes a viernes.
example.en: She works from Monday to Friday.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you say “not only X, but also Y”?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use no solo before the first matching item and sino before the second.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Keep the two sides grammatically parallel. Before a full changed verb, use sino que: no solo llamó, sino que vino. También may be added after sino, but it is not required.

example.es: No solo estudia física, sino química.
example.en: She studies not only physics, but also chemistry.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: deconstruction is a literary and philosophical approach that examines unstable meanings and oppositions within texts
cardDefinitions.noteEn: The panel imitates dense theoretical language by claiming that deconstruction cannot be separated from either the text or the self. The title text extends the joke by pointing readers to a difficult encyclopedia article on the topic.

cardDefinitions.promptEs: hobby · falso experto · disciplinas · segundos y minutos
cardDefinitions.answerEn: the speaker tests how long graduate students in different fields take to notice that he is bluffing
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Each panel gives an obviously ill-informed contribution and records the detection time. The literary-criticism group remains unconvinced only after eight papers and two books, which is the final escalation of the joke.

regions.labelEs: MI HOBBY: SENTARME CON ESTUDIANTES DE POSGRADO Y CONTAR CUÁNTO TARDAN EN DARSE CUENTA DE QUE NO SOY UN EXPERTO EN SU MATERIA.

applications.explanationEn: Me is attached to the unchanged action sentar and identifies the speaker as the person who will sit down.
Sentarme carries the matching me for the person who sits, and con introduces the students who join that action.
Cuánto keeps its accent because it introduces an embedded question about the amount of time.
Tardan gives the time-taking verb, en introduces the action, and darse cuenta supplies the realization action whose duration is measured.
Darse and cuenta form the realization expression, while de que opens the fact that becomes clear.

applications.exampleEs: SOY UN EXPERTO EN SU MATERIA
applications.explanationEn: Soy supplies the form of ser, experto names the claimed level of knowledge, en introduces the field, and su materia supplies that field.

regions.labelEs: NUESTRO GRAN PROBLEMA ES LA DISIPACIÓN DE CALOR.

words.geometryRationale: Vision read only ON and clipped the opening C; this measured box covers the complete printed CON without taking LOGARITMOS.

applications.explanationEn: Habéis is the informal-plural helper and probado is probar's completed-action form.
Habéis is the present-perfect helper used for informal plural “you,” a form especially common in Spain.
Probado gives the attempted action, con introduces the proposed option, and logaritmos fills that option slot.

excludedUnits.rationale: 48 is the measured number of seconds rather than a Spanish lexical word.
excludedUnits.geometryRationale: Vision read 148 by absorbing the nearby box edge; this measured box isolates the two printed digits 48.

regions.labelEs: ENTONCES ¿LA FAMILIA UGROFINESA ESTA INCLUYE, POR EJEMPLO, AL KLINGON?

excludedUnits.rationale: KLINGON is the unchanged proper name of a fictional constructed language, not Spanish vocabulary; the linked concept explains why it is the joke's category error.

applications.explanationEn: Familia names the category first, and ugrofinesa follows as its neutral descriptive classification.
Ugrofinesa uses feminine singular -a because it describes the feminine singular noun familia.
Por and ejemplo form the conventional expression that introduces one illustrative member of a category.

excludedUnits.rationale: 63 is the measured number of seconds rather than a Spanish lexical word.

regions.labelEs: SÍ, MI ÚLTIMO TRABAJO CONSISTE EN CLASIFICAR A LA GENTE DE LA MEJOR A LA PEOR.

applications.explanationEn: Consiste introduces the definition, en links it to the activity, and clasificar stays in its unchanged -ar form.
A marks the people as the direct affected target, while la gente names that human group.

applications.exampleEs: DE LA MEJOR A LA PEOR
applications.explanationEn: De introduces the best-ranked endpoint and a introduces the worst-ranked endpoint; each adjective keeps its feminine article because it stands for a feminine person in the group.

excludedUnits.rationale: 4 is the measured number of minutes rather than a Spanish lexical word.

applications.explanationEn: Crítica names the field first, and literaria follows to classify it by its subject matter.
Literaria uses feminine singular -a because it describes the feminine singular noun crítica.

regions.labelEs: VERÁS, LA DECONSTRUCCIÓN ES INEXTRICABLE NO SOLO DEL TEXTO, SINO DEL SER.

applications.exampleEs: NO SOLO DEL TEXTO, SINO DEL SER
applications.explanationEn: No solo marks del texto as the first parallel item, and sino adds the matching second item del ser.

regions.labelEs: OCHO PAPERS Y DOS LIBROS Y TODAVÍA NO SE HAN PERCATADO.

applications.explanationEn: Todavía keeps the situation open up to the current point, and no makes the expected realization remain absent.
Han is the plural present-perfect helper and percatado is percatarse's completed-action form; the preceding se supplies the matching marker for that verb.
